issues.description: The template exports the symbol 'main' (global main) while the solution exports '_start' (global _start). The provided Makefile links the object with gcc (which expects a 'main' symbol from the C runtime). Changing the global symbol to '_start' in the solution creates a visibility/entry-point mismatch that can cause linking errors or unexpected behavior when using the supplied Makefile and the template structure. Students will be confused about which symbol to implement/export and may get linker errors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the entry-point symbol consistent between template and solution. Either change the solution to export 'main' (use 'global main') so it matches the template and the gcc-based Makefile, or update the Makefile and template to correctly use a custom '_start' entry (and remove/avoid linking the C runtime). Preferably revert the solution to 'global main' to preserve the original template linking process.

issues.description: The template declares the program entry symbol with 'global main' while the solution file declares 'global _start'. These refer to the same conceptual entity (the module's exported entry symbol) but use different identifiers across artifacts, which can confuse students about which global symbol is required for linking with the toolchain and which label they should implement or preserve.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the exported entry symbol name across artifacts. Prefer changing 'global _start' in solution_repository/pixel.asm to 'global main' so it matches the template and the expected C runtime entry point used by the Makefile/linker; alternatively, change the template to use 'global _start' and document the different entry point, but keeping 'global main' is recommended for consistency with the template and GCC linking.
